chunks: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said to Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī:

“The four mosques are: al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Masjid Bayt al-Maqdis, and Masjid al-Kūfah. O Abū Ḥamzah, the obligatory prayer in them equals a hajj, and the supererogatory prayer equals an ‘umrah.”

key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ: the four specially distinguished mosques mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.حَجَّةً: the reward equivalent of a hajj in this context
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in Madinah
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْكُوفَةِ: the mosque of Kufah, identified as one of the four virtuous mosques
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ: the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis in Jerusalem

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the four sacred mosques mentioned by Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies four especially virtuous mosques: al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, Masjid al-Rasūl صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Bayt al-Maqdis, and Masjid al-Kūfah. It states that performing an obligatory salat in these mosques carries the reward of a hajj, while a supererogatory prayer in them carries the reward of an ‘umrah.
